_instructions.about: Your CV. The About page renders this file automatically, so edit text here and push; no HTML changes needed. Publications and Presentations are pulled from publications.json and presentations.json, so add papers there and they show up on the CV too. To refresh the downloadable PDF, run ./tools/build-cv-pdf.sh and commit assets/VishalJohnCV.pdf.

section types.entries: A list of positions. Each item: title, org, location (optional), dates, note (optional, one line in italics), bullets (optional list).
section types.list: A simple list of lines. Each item: text, and optionally dates.
section types.skills: Labeled groups. Each item: label, text.
section types.source: Set "source": "publications" or "presentations" to pull from those JSON files.

tips: Reorder sections by moving them in the sections list.
Delete a whole item to hide it; set "hidden": true on an item or section to keep it in the file but not show it.
Wrap text in **double stars** to make it bold.

name: Vishal John
headline: M.D. Candidate, Class of 2028 · University of Louisville School of Medicine

items.title: Doctor of Medicine (M.D.) Candidate
items.org: University of Louisville School of Medicine

items.title: B.S., Biopsychology, Cognition, and Neuroscience
items.note: Minor in Business Administration, Ross School of Business

items.title: Clinical Research Technician
items.org: Koschmann Lab for Pediatric Brain Cancer, Michigan Medicine, Pediatric Hematology/Oncology
bullets: Quantified circulating tumor DNA in CSF, plasma, and tissue from pediatric brain tumor patients by ddPCR to track response during ONC201 clinical trials.
Developed a stem cell-derived thalamic and cortical organoid co-culture model of diffuse midline glioma invasion; presented as first author at the BioInnovation in Brain Cancer Symposium.
Coordinated autopsy tissue and biofluid collection and built a barcoded tracking system for the lab's biorepository.
Maintained IRB approval for human subjects studies and trained lab members in ddPCR, qPCR, western blot, organoid culture, cryosectioning, confocal microscopy, IHC, and ELISA.

items.title: Project Lead
bullets: Led the Citizen Scientist Sequencing Initiative, in which high school students sequence their own DNA and analyze variants of interest; presented this work at ASHG 2025.
Directed a small RNA-seq research pipeline on Alzheimer's disease and mentored students in R, Linux, cutadapt, bowtie, samtools, and DESeq.
Wrote and secured grant funding and managed partner and vendor relationships.

items.title: Research & Teaching Assistant
bullets: Taught high school students computational biology (GEO2R, STRING, R); mentored 68 students to publish research abstracts.
Ran a 4-hour computational biology contest for 164 students from across the Midwest and California.

items.title: Bluegrass Biodesign, Cardiology / Cardiothoracic Surgery Team
items.org: University of Louisville School of Medicine & J.B. Speed School of Engineering
bullets: Identified an unmet clinical need through clinical observation and physician interviews, then designed, prototyped, and tested a device with an engineering team.
Completed customer discovery and business training through UofL's NSF I-Corps program.

items.text: **John V**, Patel N. *The Brave Little Immune Team*. Children's book introducing the immune system to ages 4–8. 2025. Available on Amazon.

items.title: President
items.org: Oncology Interest Group, University of Louisville School of Medicine

items.title: Leadership Team
bullets: Free rock climbing for children and young adults with cancer. Built the program's website and merchandise shop and helped grow it to national coverage on NBC Nightly News and mlive.
Helped launch the Louisville program in partnership with Norton Children's Cancer Institute; volunteer belayer.

items.title: President
items.org: Genes in Diseases and Symptoms (GIDAS), University of Michigan
bullets: Raised over $27,000 for disease research microgrants and organized a monthly speaker series with physicians and scientists.

items.title: Volunteer
bullets: Supported a free screening fair (blood pressure, diabetes, vision) for Louisville's Asian Pacific community, entertaining children with balloon art so families could be screened.

items.title: Volunteer
items.org: Hospital Elder Life Program (HELP), Michigan Medicine
